short: The Grainyhead/CP2 family binds the palindrome AACCGGTT through an immunoglobulin-like DNA-binding domain that shares a fold with p53 but differs from it in important details. Six human members split into two branches: the epithelial GRHL1, GRHL2 and GRHL3, and the more broadly expressed TFCP2 (LSF/CP2), TFCP2L1 and UBP1 (LBP-1a). They bind as dimers, and many real elements are doubled, giving 16-26 bp tandem sites. GRHL factors control epidermal barrier formation, neural tube and palate closure, and epithelial identity, and they sit at the epithelial end of EMT regulation. Human mutations cause Van der Woude syndrome and nonsyndromic cleft palate.
long:
## The factors

Six human genes belong to this family. The grainyhead-like branch, GRHL1, GRHL2 and GRHL3, is
epithelial: GRHL1 and GRHL3 in epidermis and periderm, GRHL2 in most simple and stratified
epithelia including airway, gut and bladder. The CP2 branch, TFCP2 (also LSF or CP2), TFCP2L1
(CRTR-1) and UBP1 (LBP-1a), is more broadly expressed and includes the factor originally
characterized on the alpha-globin promoter. All six share a roughly 250-residue region that carries
both DNA binding and dimerization, inherited from Drosophila Grainyhead (also called NTF-1 and
Elf-1), and the Drosophila and human domains are interchangeable enough that the family was
recognized by that conservation. Crystal structures of the GRHL1 and GRHL2 DNA-binding domains
showed a closely similar immunoglobulin-like core sharing the overall fold of the p53 DNA-binding
domain while differing in the DNA-contacting elements. GRHL1 binds its recognition element as a
dimer, and target-site selection is parsimonious: two conserved arginine residues make most of
the base-specific contacts.

## The motif

The consensus is the 8-bp palindrome AACCGGTT, often written with flanking A/T as AAACCGGTTT.
Because selection rests on a small number of arginine contacts, the central CCGG is the most
constrained part and the flanking AA/TT contribute the rest. The palindrome means the two halves
are equivalent, and dimer binding is the normal mode. A conspicuous feature of this family's
models is doubling: HOCOMOCO entries for TFCP2, TFCP2L1, UBP1 and GRHL3 span 15-26 columns and
contain two AACCGGTT-like units, sometimes in the arrangement AACCGGTT-N(2)-AACCGGTT. That is a
genuine property of Grh/CP2 elements rather than a modelling artifact, and it is why the highest
information content in this family (about 20 bits) comes from CP2-branch models rather than from
the single-site GRHL models. Degenerate variants are common and legitimate: AACAGGTT, AACTGGTT and
AACCAGTT all appear as database consensuses, reflecting tolerance at the central positions. No
member is reliably distinguishable from another by sequence. The GRHL and CP2 branches are similar
enough that Vierstra collapses them into archetypes named GRHL/TFCP, and this family's cohesion
(0.78) is limited mainly by the mixture of single-site and doubled models, not by disagreement
about the core.

## Where it acts

Grh/CP2 sites occur at both promoters and enhancers, with a strong bias toward epithelial
differentiation loci: the epidermal differentiation complex, tight junction and desmosome genes,
transglutaminases, and the genes of the cornified envelope. GRHL3 binding is highly dynamic, with
enhancer usage rearranging as keratinocytes move between proliferative and differentiating states.
GRHL2 also occupies enhancers in pluripotent cells during exit from naive pluripotency and in
airway basal cells during mucociliary regeneration. Common neighbors are KLF4 and TP63 in
keratinocytes, IRF6 in periderm (GRHL3 and IRF6 act in the same genetic pathway for oral periderm),
and AP-1 at differentiation enhancers. GRHL factors recruit Trithorax-group complexes to switch on
differentiation genes, and in cancer they sit in a mutually repressive loop with ZEB1 and the
miR-200 family that keeps cells epithelial. The palindrome is 8 bp, so chance matches are frequent;
doubled sites are much rarer and much more indicative.

## Biology and disease

Grhl3-null mice fail to form a skin permeability barrier and develop spina bifida that is
resistant to both inositol and folate supplementation, identifying Grhl3 as the gene behind the
long-studied curly tail mouse. Grhl3 is also required for eyelid closure and urothelial
differentiation. In humans, dominant GRHL3 mutations cause Van der Woude syndrome, the commonest
syndromic form of cleft lip and palate, in families without IRF6 mutations; separate GRHL3 coding
variants, including a common susceptibility allele and rare truncating variants, cause and predispose
to nonsyndromic cleft palate. GRHL2 variants are associated with age-related hearing impairment,
and GRHL2 has both oncogenic and tumor-suppressive effects depending on context, promoting the
epithelial phenotype in breast, ovarian and prostate cancer while restraining metastatic
dissemination. TFCP2 appears in cancer as a fusion partner: EWSR1-TFCP2 and FUS-TFCP2 fusions define
an aggressive intraosseous spindle and epithelioid rhabdomyosarcoma with frequent ALK
overexpression, often in the jaw and skull.

## Reading a hit

An AACCGGTT match identifies the Grh/CP2 family and no individual member. That matters because the
two branches have different biology: a hit could correspond to epithelial GRHL2 or to broadly
expressed TFCP2, and only expression or ChIP data can tell you which. At 8 bp with a palindromic
core, single matches occur often by chance, so treat a lone AACCGGTT the way you would treat any
8-mer: as a hypothesis. A doubled site, two AACCGGTT-like units within about 20 bp, is a much
stronger signal and is the form in which many validated elements occur. Also note that models in
this family differ in width by a factor of three, from 8 to 26 columns, so scores from different
databases are not comparable and a "weaker" hit may simply reflect a narrower model. The evidence
base is mixed but reasonable: several HOCOMOCO models for GRHL1, GRHL3, TFCP2, TFCP2L1 and UBP1
rest on in vitro selection (evidence codes SM, SB, S), which supports direct binding, whereas the
GRHL2 models here are ChIP-only (P) and their degenerate variants (AACAGGTT, CCGGTTTGGCCAG) should
be read as descriptions of GRHL2 peaks rather than of GRHL2's intrinsic specificity.
caveats: A hit names the family, not the member, and the family spans two branches with different expression: epithelial GRHL1-3 versus broadly expressed TFCP2, TFCP2L1 and UBP1. The 8-bp palindrome occurs frequently by chance, so single matches are weak; doubled AACCGGTT units within about 20 bp are much more convincing. Model widths in this family range from 8 to 26 columns, so scores across databases are not comparable. Degenerate variants such as AACAGGTT come mostly from ChIP-only GRHL2 models and describe peak composition rather than intrinsic specificity; the in vitro-supported models converge on AACCGGTT.
